#1260. Police arrest seven men after Man United's 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool at Anfield - with two suspected of illegal tragedy chanting

Published: 03:43 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:45 EST, 24 November 2026

Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.

But even before the visitors saw Leny Yoro sent off and four conceded without reply, this fixture has long been one of the most incendiary in the top flight.

Supporters arrested for suspected tragedy chanting are thought to be a 63-year-old man from Heywood, Greater Manchester, and a 57-year-old man from Wallasey, in Wirral, as per the Athletic.

Both clubs have waged independent battles against tragedy chanting, which sees fans taunt opponents by mocking major disasters, such as Hillsborough, the Heysel Stadium disaster, and the Munich air disaster.

Some tragedy chants are even aimed at the personal lives of players on the pitch, and in 2024, new guidance from the Crown Prosecution saw tragedy chanting upgraded to a criminal offence.

Seven people have been arrested following Man United's trip to face Liverpool at Anfield (police pictured breaking up a fight in the away end)

As well as tragedy chanting, a 47-year-old man from Swinton, Greater Manchester, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a class A drug.

Two men - a 49-year-old from Didsbury, South Manchester, and a 38-year-old from Denton, Greater Manchester - were arrested on suspicion of indecent and racialist chanting.

A further two, aged 30 and 23, were arrested during the final minutes of Sunday's clash as a skirmish broke out among the away supporters at Anfield.

But despite the enmity between the two teams, there were a greater number of arrests last month, when Man City visited Anfield for the first match in the wake of the revelation that the club had been found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them for breaching the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

That fixture saw 10 fans arrested, with five arrested on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The match-up between the two sides became increasingly charged with the establishment of a rivalry at the top of the table under former managers Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola.

In 2018, the Man City bus was attacked with bottles, bricks and flares ahead of a Champions League meeting between the two sides, with future fixtures in Liverpool at times seeing the players' bus route amended to avoid throngs of home fans.

In March 2025, Merseyside police requested an unorthodox kick-off of 3.45pm for the match, rather than the customary Sunday start time of 4.30pm, in a bid to reduce issues between the two sets of fans.

#1259. PSG coach Enrique pinpoints Roma threat and praises Gasperini for ‘clear playing identity’

Luis Enrique has warned Paris Saint-Germain that Roma will cause them problems in the Champions League on Wednesday, and praised Gian Piero Gasperini for building teams with a “very clear playing identity”.

With quotes via PSG’s official website, the Spaniard was speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Wednesday’s league-phase clash at the Parc des Princes. Kick-off is at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT].

The two sides are heading in very different directions in Europe. PSG sit top of the league phase with a perfect record of 12 points from four matches, having scored 20 goals and conceded just five, while Roma are 20th with four points.

“It’s clear we’re happy to be back in the Champions League, and above all at home,” Luis Enrique said. “This match will be very different from what we’ve experienced so far. They’re a team that defends in a particular way, but we can’t wait.

“They’re a team that loses very few matches. We know it will be very difficult, and it’ll be a great challenge. If we win this game, it’ll be the first time we’ve won five matches in a row in the league phase, so that would be a first!”

Luis Enrique had plenty of praise for Gasperini. The two crossed paths in 2011, when the Spaniard was in charge at Roma and Gasperini lasted only a few weeks at Inter.

“He’s a coach with a lot of experience, and I like him a lot. His teams have a very clear playing identity, very different from what we’re used to coming up against,” he said.

“I remember he was at Inter when I was coaching Roma. It was complicated for him there, but he proved afterwards what he was capable of. We know they’ll cause us problems tomorrow, and it’s a great challenge.”

The holders will be without two of their biggest names. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during PSG’s win over Barcelona last month, and Désiré Doué also faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a suspected ACL injury.

“That’s football at the highest level. Every team and every coach goes through it. There are injuries,” Luis Enrique said. “It’s very sad to have this type of injury for players like Désiré and Kvara, but we’re focusing on their recovery and how we can improve our performance.

“This team has shown all its resilience over the last three years. We’ve always bounced back from everything.”

He also ruled out signing a short-term replacement in January.

“We don’t have to sign anyone in the transfer window, and it’s not our style to sign a player for six months. We’re happy with our squad. Above all, we’re not afraid of anything. We’re confident in our ability and our resilience.”

The former Roma coach was also asked about his time in the Italian capital.

“My time at Roma was very special for me, and I have great memories. It’s a magnificent city, I experienced some lovely things there as a coach, and I’m at peace with everything that happened to me there.”

#1258. Leeds United Can Convince Celtic to Sell 'Best Striker' Durán with Right Offer

Leeds United may be able to tempt a cash-hungry Celtic board into selling a prize asset if they are willing to spend a significant chunk. The Whites are said to be interested in Celtic frontman Camilo Durán, who has dazzled since joining the Scottish club in the summer.

Durán joined the Hoops for a bargain £5.5million deal from Qarabag after netting five times in the Champions League last season, and he has hit the ground running. The forward has scored 14 goals across all competitions, and he has found the net just as regularly in the Europa League as in the Scottish Premiership.

He has even been a consistent scorer when starting on the right wing, where he has often found himself to make room for centre-forward Kasper Hogh, who arrived on an £11million deal but has only scored three times and is now more than three months without a goal.

And don't be fooled by Celtic's competition. The Hoops signed right-winger Haissem Hassan for £6million - which could raise to £9million - during the summer window, with the Egypt international having impressed during the World Cup, but he is without a goal up to this point, so even other higher quality players are not having the success in front of goal from the same positions Durán is operating in. And that's a big part of the reason clubs like Leeds are said to be scouting the Colombian.

But Celtic's reliance on Durán means it's going to be hard to lure the Colombian away from Parkhead, especially during the season. A January deal is going to be particularly difficult to strike, although there may be a slither of hope if Celtic are eliminated from the Europa League before then. The Bhoys currently have three points after four games and will need six or seven points from their last four to extend their European campaign.

That could be a key factor, but in any case, a summer deal remains realistic if Leeds are willing to pay north of £15million, which would give Celtic the chance of tripling their £5.5million investment in the space of just one year.

"I believe he is the future of Colombian football and he should be first pick in our team. For me, he is the best striker we have." - Arnulfo Valentierra (Durán's former Independiente Medellín manager) speaking this season.

This Celtic board has previously turned down big money in the January window, blocking the £25million exit of Arne Engels last January, but they sold him for £3million less in the summer when West Ham came calling. They never replaced the midfielder, either, leaving fans furious amid an ongoing civil war between them and the board over a perceived lack of ambition.

“We are building a team here and guys like Camilo are part of the future. He has a lot of talent.” - Nestor Lorenzo (Colombia head coach)

This Celtic board likes to turn a profit, and it is willing to do it at the cost of the team to a certain degree. Another sale could complicate things, and Benjamin Nygren is the leading candidate to leave next summer as things stand, but if Leeds can get in early and make a sizable offer for Durán, the bargain deal he arrived at Celtic on will give them a chance of sealing a deal, as long as they are willing to stump up a sizable amount of cash compared to that initial £5.5million fee.

Camilo Duran has been in electric form for Celtic and Leeds United have been scouting the 14-goal man this season

#1257. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso)

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

#1256. £35m Star's Man Utd Career is Already Over After Pochettino's First Match

Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of Manchester United couldn't have gone any worse, and the writing is already on the wall for a number of players following the Argentine's first 90 minutes in the dugout as he sets about trying to revolutionise Man United.

Pochettino arrived in Manchester last week knowing that a point would probably be enough to take the club out of the Premier League's relegation zone, and he set up his team to get at least that when they face Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

However, his game plan was ripped up eight minutes into the match when Leny Yoro was red-carded after being adjudged to have brought down Alexander Isak as the last man outside the penalty area.

If Pochettino wasn't fully aware of his side's defensive shortcomings before taking over, he is now, and the club now have the worst defensive record out of every club in Europe's top five European leagues.

Luke Shaw wasn't even involved on Merseyside, but he might now be undroppable after what the former Spurs boss witnessed against Andoni Iraola's men, as Diogo Dalot once again struggled out of position at left-back.

Yoro continues to flatter to deceive following a big-money move from Lille, while Matthijs de Ligt and Lisandro Martinez both endured nightmare afternoons against Liverpool.

The latter seems likely to leave Old Trafford in 2027 given his contract expires at the end of the season, and given he publicly spoke out against Jason Wilcox's recruitment following the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid last month.

The Argentina international was fined and given a 'dressing down' by Wilcox, according to one report, and it's difficult to see why they would want to keep him around beyond next summer.

Martinez isn't the only United player whose Old Trafford career could be over though, especially when you consider Joshua Zirkzee's situation.

There was excitement when United signed Joshua Zirkzee from Bologna for £35m in 2024, given his level of performance for the Serie A outfit and the fact that he had shown he was a player capable of the spectacular.

However, the Netherlands international quickly lost the manager who signed him, Erik ten Hag, when he was sacked in October 2024, and has failed to convince Ruben Amorim or Michael Carrick since that he was worthy of regular minutes on the pitch.

Even in the absence of the injured Benjamin Sesko in recent months, when Carrick had no other recognised striker to turn to, Zirkzee was still often left on the substitutes' bench.

Now, the Times have reported that, despite their defensive issues, United have prioritised signing a new striker in January, such is their concerns about how things have gone without Sesko.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is keen to be reunited with Pochettino having worked with him during the duo's time with the United States national team.

With Sesko also due back from his shin injury in January or February, Zirkzee will be left as the third-choice option if he remains at Old Trafford beyond January.

The 25-year-old may have been given 45 minutes at Anfield on Sunday, but he failed to make much of an impact, albeit in difficult circumstances after his side were reduced to 10 men so early in the game.

Given how things have gone this season for Zirkzee, coupled with his limited minutes under the previous two managers, the fact that United are prioritising a new striker over defenders tells you all you need to know - his United career is over.

#1255. Rabiot matches Kaká feat as Milan seek to get extension over the line

Adrien Rabiot has joined Ricardo Kaká in Milan’s history books, and the Rossoneri are now working to tie the Frenchman down to a new long-term contract.

According to Pianeta Milan, Rabiot became the first Milan midfielder since 2004-05 to be directly involved in at least one goal in seven consecutive Serie A appearances. The last Rossoneri player to manage a similar run was Kaká.

Rabiot extended that streak with two assists in Sunday’s 5-1 win over Frosinone, setting up Gonçalo Ramos and Ardon Jashari. He also delivered the ball that led to Gabriele Calvani’s own goal.

The 31-year-old now has five goals and six assists this season. That makes him the first Serie A midfielder in 20 years to reach 10 or more goal involvements in his first 10 league games of a campaign. He’s also the only central midfielder across Europe’s top five leagues to have already passed that mark this term.

Milan have every reason to reward him, with the Frenchman’s current deal running until June 2028 and worth €3.5 million net per season.

The club hope to have a new contract signed before Christmas, although the paperwork could slip into the new year. The extension is expected to run until June 2030, with an option for a further season. Rabiot’s salary would rise to €5m net plus bonuses, putting him level with Mike Maignan and Gonçalo Ramos as one of the squad’s top earners.

Ruben Amorim made his own feelings clear after Sunday’s win, calling Rabiot “one of the best midfielders in Europe” and saying he hopes the renewal comes soon.

hahahahaha he is no Kaka. He’d have lasted 5mins in the Serie A back then

#1254. Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

England’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

The visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh

It was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof

Kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

These could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

The concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

The goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z

England were swarming all over Croatia. Saka crossed, Gordon took the ball down and turned it back for Bellingham to stab home.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M

Gordon, after twice being denied, got his goal – with another header, as against the Czechs. This time Jarell Quansah, back in ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, delivered from the right and Gordon met it to score for the fourth successive game for England. Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

After the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

Saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. Maybe three minutes after the three-zero there was a big mistake [Kovacic’s chance] and some easy ball losses but that was a performance of the highest level from everyone. And from the first until the last minute from everyone who started and everyone who came on. Congratulations to the team.

Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

Unbelievable from start to finish. We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game in which we were dominant with and without the ball and that was it out there. We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

There’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

Beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,

[And now to equal Peter Shilton’s record 125th cap on Tuesday?] That would be nice. That’s why he keeps taking me off, to rest me for the next game. That’s what he said to me after. I’ll be ready to start on Tuesday.

An amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

It was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

We showed the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

[Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.

At least the Croatia fans did not seem too dispirited, the kids smiling and waving at the camera, despite the utter trouncing their team took.

England were terrific but how much of that was because Croatia were terrible will be open to debate.

Eze just overcooks the pass that would have released Gibbs-White to run through on goal.

That was Bellingham’s third assist and should it stay 7-0 after two minutes of stoppage time, it will be Croatia’s heaviest defeat.

England really ought to be in double figures by now.

Sucic is penalised for a sliding tackle on Bellingham that legs up the England forward in full flight down the left. Saka takes it, crossing on a shallow arc to the 18-yard line. Guéhi cushions a header but too close to a defender for Kane to pounce.

Anderson takes the corner short and Croatia defend the belated cross.

Looks like the Croatian kids were busy in art and English classed this week, as they unfurled a banner that read ‘It’s not coming home’ in one side of the ground as the game kicked off.

England attack up the left patiently, turning back when necessary. Kane drops deep and fires a pass to Bellingham who plays it down the inside-left for Gordon who runs beyond Vuskovic and rakes a left-foot shot that Livakovic, his Cam Nou team-mate, turns behind.

Alex Scott is given the first kick of the game, knocks it all the way back to Pickford who pumps it so long that Livakovic comes for it and makes a mess of it, shanking it out for a throw-in.

The Croatia national anthem is belted out. Croatia are heart-clutchers when they sing their anthem. It seems an increasingly common practice.

And it does sound like a schoolboy international. England are in red shirts and navy shorts, Croatia in their white and red chequerboard.

You can hear the players singing the national anthem.

Three sides of the ground are now full of small children – and some bigger children who look suspiciously like adults. There’s every chance that I either end this game with a headache or running away from a pack of dogs, given the high-pitched home support.

I just watched Anthony Barry put on a finishing drill with some of the England players. The standard was pretty high, but the quality of Kane’s finishing was, unsurprisingly, superb. He scored with seven of his eight shots past James Trafford and Jason Steele. The one shot he didn’t score with forced Steele into an excellent save. You often see players go through the motions in the pre-match warm-up, but not Kane. He hit every shot like he was trying to win the game in the 90th minute. England’s starters have now gone in ahead of kick-off.

[The camp] has been very good, helped us unwind and recharge the batteries after two intense matches. We have been on the road for a few days, the setting was beautiful. Now we need to switch on which is very difficult [because] the atmosphere is very different with 6,000 children in the stadium. We want to make it a really competitive game but the surrounding is very different. I think wee are up for it.

[Alex Scott] did so well in training and did so well when he made his debut so he brings the full package. He has legs, good at defending, good in the high press, smooth on the ball and good decision-making. That is why he has our trust.

It was a close decision [over Alexander-Arnold] but we decided for Jarrell to start. We will have a lot to defend especially on that side with Perisic and Jarrell did well with Bukayo. We have Trent as an option from the bench.

We need a complete performance in all aspects, adapt to the circumstances. Our physicality, if it is a real competitive match then we would have the edge. Now it feels more like an open training session with the environment and that will suit them better.

But I hope we can bring the intensity and then have the edge.

"To be fair, I don't care" 🤷‍♂️😂Never change, Slaven Bilić 🇭🇷 pic.twitter.com/hBrtZ5TiBy

Loud (high-pitched) cheers for the Croatia team from children inside the Rijeka Stadium. Luka Modric, aged 41, is starting for the home team. He’s a year older than Wayne Rooney, who retired from international football nine years ago. The England players were booed when they entered the pitch. These kids know what they are doing.

I was here eight years ago when it really was a behind-closed-doors game for England. This is very different. There are around 6,000 Croatian children, with their guardians, here and the stands are filling up. It’s also pretty noisy with all the pre-match music.

In 2018, we could hear exactly what the managers and players were shouting – Jordan Henderson was particularly loud – but I don’t think that will be the case this time around. The noise from the fans may be quite high pitched today, but I don’t think it will be quiet at all.

England have 100 fans here and, mercifully, they have not been forced to watch from inside the metal caged away end. They haven’t been allowed to bring in England flags, so it’s currently quite hard to locate exactly where they are.

Thomas Tuchel was glowing about Alex Scott in his pre-match media duties ahead of today’s game against Croatia and the midfielder has been handed his first England start.

Scott has come in for Myles Lewis-Skelly in what looks to be an attacking change from Tuchel, the England head coach.

Tuchel had taken Scott to the United States on his pre-World Cup training camp, but the Bournemouth midfielder was not part of the squad for the tournament-proper.

On Scott, Tuchel said: “I am super impressed by Alex Scott, I think he is at the moment one of the best central midfielders in the Premier League and he just proves it in every training session. He had a fantastic debut the other day and really really impressed me.”

🇭🇷🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Croatia's starting XI vs. England!Petar Musa and Martin Baturina get their first starts under Slaven Bilić! pic.twitter.com/dPt32fiXbh

Jordan Pickford has revealed he spends up to three hours talking to a “mindwork coach”.

The England goalkeeper has worked with sports psychologists for some time but has gone into detail about how committed he is as he faces a challenge to his No 1 spot from James Trafford.

Pickford will start for England in the Nations League tie against Croatia, and next Tuesday’s fixture at home to the Czech Republic, having missed out on the past two games.

Trafford was in goal for the 3-2 loss to Spain and the 2-0 victory away to the Czechs and although Thomas Tuchel has said Pickford remains his first choice it is known that he and his coaching staff are huge admirers of Leeds United’s new goalkeeper.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

Despite Alexander-Arnold providing an assist for Anthony Gordon against the Czech Republic, England head coach Thomas Tuchel is expected to replace him with Jarell Quansah at right-back.

Jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

Uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

However, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

#1253. Tottenham Offered Chance To Sign Ivan Toney, De Zerbi Needs Him

After signing 10 new players in the summer across all areas of the pitch, you would think that Tottenham Hotspur's squad is in a strong state.

It would be fair to say that there is good depth across the defence and midfield in particular, with Marcos Senesi and Luca Williams-Barnett coming into the starting XI against Ipswich Town on Saturday and producing performances that make them undroppable against Sunderland next time out.

Tottenham have now won three successive Premier League matches for the first time in nearly two years, and they are now in the top half of the table having been rock-bottom earlier in the season.

Spurs are certainly improving but there is still a way to go to get to where they want to be under Roberto De Zerbi, who signed a long-term contract to build a project at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

While the north London outfit have looked strong defensively in recent matches, conceding 11 in 11 top flight matches this term, their goalscoring is more of a concern.

Saturday's double against the Tractor Boys took their tally to 12 in 11, but they need to be better than that if they want to really push on and be in contention for a European spot this term.

De Zerbi has had a striker conundrum all season, having begun the campaign with Richarlison in the centre-forward position, even though the Brazilian had informed during the summer that he wanted to leave the club.

After failing to secure a move away from Spurs, the former Everton attacker remains exiled and on the sidelines, while Dominic Solanke continues to fail to show that he is the consistent goalscorer needed.

De Zerbi has used Omar Marmoush in the striker role too, following his summer move from Manchester City, but the Egyptian international has also failed to fire there, and it's difficult to see exactly where he fits in.

It's becoming apparent that the Italian boss needs extra competition for Solanke, and TEAMtalk report that they have been contacted about the potential availability of Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney by intermediaries.

If De Zerbi wants a striker who has proven he can put the ball in the back of the net regularly in January, there might not be many better options than the England international.

The report claims that the 30-year-old is weighing up a return to England in the New Year, with intermediaries proposing a loan move featuring an option to buy, if Al-Ahli would be willing to agree to that.

A number of Premier League clubs are said to have been contacted by those intermediaries, including Tottenham, Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United.

New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank is also keen to be reunited with Toney having worked with him at Brentford previously, and that would probably be the landing spot where he'd be guaranteed the most minutes.

Even though Toney has moved to Saudi Arabia, he has continued to be prolific and he has 16 goals in 17 appearances for Al-Ahli this term.

Such has been his form in Saudi that former Al-Ahli sporting director Rui Pedro labelled him 'one of the best strikers in the world', while his England teammate Declan Rice has also been full of praise for him in the past.

Toney's England call-ups followed on from his performances and numbers for Brentford, and his goalscoring form has continued ever since.

He's kind of like Harry Kane in a way where he's not only an out-and-out striker, he's a playmaker as well - his left and right footed passing, the way he picks out his teammates is a special technique to have.

Toney has proven that he can score regularly in the Premier League, and it will be interesting to see who wins the race to bring him back to the Premier League if it's a move that does become possible in the winter market.

#1252. Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: Full VAR Audio Transcript of Leny Yoro’s Red Card

The full VAR audio transcript has been released for Leny Yoro's controversial red card during Manchester United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday afternoon.

It took just eight minutes for Mauricio Pochettino's honeymoon period as the new Red Devils' boss to come to a blow, with the French defender being dismissed for allegedly denying Alexander Isak of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Two minutes later, and Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free-kick, before further goals from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha, and substitute Victor Munoz condemned the visitors to a chastening loss.

United now sit 19th in the Premier League table, having won just one of their 11 league fixtures this season. And now, after former PGMOL chief Keith Hackett claimed referee Sam Barrott made an incorrect decision, with the FA since rescinding Yoro's red card, the VAR audio during a turning point in United's season makes for an interesting listen.

Reviewing the footage to see whether Yoro had denied Isak of a goalscoring opportunity, it has now been confirmed that those at Stockley Park did take into consideration whether the striker was still in control of the ball and able to get on the end of his loose touch, despite many believing that was the one factor that made Barrott's decision an incorrect call.

"Go back to 18 yards. Let's roll it through, firstly to see whether the striker is going to get on to the end of the ball," the VAR begins saying to the referee.

"Just roll it through, real speed. So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and is likely to get on the end of the ball, ok. Certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn't. So I think the DOGSO is confirmed, we'll just check APP (Attacking possession phase."

Early red for Yoro divides opinion as Isak's minimal contact fuels claims the VAR call was unjust and pundits expect an apology.

The clip lasts just 22 seconds, with Barrott agreeing with the VAR during the entire, very quick, process. But the judgement is certainly expected to draw more criticism on social media given the views and opinions of other pundits and rule experts.

There's no other way to truly describe United's current situation as anything but a disaster. After shipping four goals at Anfield - something they also achieved in a 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa and a 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como - no other team in Europe's top five leagues has conceded more than their 34 goals.

Manchester United have conceded 34 goals across all competitions this season, which has made defence a priority in January.

In the Premier League, they find themselves 11 points worse than West Ham did at this stage of last season, and the Hammers were subsequently relegated into the Championship. Meanwhile, this year's division feels far more stronger.

Of course, it's all well and good saying United have the resources to make sure relegation doesn't ever happen, with Old Trafford's top brass now increasingly likely to splash out on new defenders in January - but the reality right now is that Pochettino's side are in deep trouble.

#1251. Fabregas issues hands-off warning for Como talent Nico Paz: ‘They’ve already come to sign him but he’s ours’

Cesc Fabregas has admitted that clubs have already tried to sign Nico Paz, but insists the Argentine is going nowhere for now.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, the Como coach was speaking to TNT Sports Mexico and was asked whether any of Europe’s giants had come knocking for the 22-year-old.

“They’ve already come here to take him,” Fabregas said with a laugh. “For three years I’ve heard people around here saying he’s going to leave, but for now I still see him here. So don’t worry, he’s our player, and we’ll see what happens.”

Paz’s future was the subject of a long saga in the summer. Real Madrid triggered their buy-back option on the player, then gave Como a preferential option to keep him. Como eventually paid around €60 million to make the move permanent, although Real Madrid kept a buy-back clause for 2027, so the question will come up again next summer.

Fabregas also talked about managing such a young dressing room, which is now competing in Serie A and the Champions League at the same time.

“I’m not just a coach. I’m here coaching 12 lads aged between 19 and 22, so I’m an educator, a father,” he said.

“I’m very clear about who we are at Como. We’re not Real Madrid, Bayern Munich or Manchester United, so we have to stay humble, respect everyone and grow at the right time.

“If one day I saw that a lad thought he was superior, or above what he really is in this context, at this club, in this team, then we wouldn’t like that any more. Because no, we’re not like that. It’s exactly the opposite.”

He also had more praise for Paz: “Nico is an exceptional boy and he has an incredible personality. I love his character and the way he sees things, and he’s a competitor. In the end, that’s what I like about him.”

Como host AEK Athens in the Champions League tonight at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT]. A win would go a long way towards securing a place in the knockout phase play-offs.

#1250. Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and said he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel said: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

But on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

“We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”

We played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find new words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

[Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone showed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

He’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

You saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

It started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it quickly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

This is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Secret to Harry Kane’s England longevity? ‘He strikes the ball better than Ronaldo’

Right foot, goal. Left foot, goal. Edge of the area, goal. Inside the area, goal. Under pressure, goal, Right foot, save. Left foot, goal. That was Harry Kane’s warm-up prior to England’s 7-0 demolition of Croatia and it underlined just why the striker will equal Peter Shilton’s appearance record on Tuesday night.

As demonstrated in Rijeka, Kane’s career has been a non-stop pursuit of excellence that has led him to the very top of the national game. England’s record goalscorer will also become the joint most-capped player with Shilton, when he makes his 125th appearance against the Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday night.

Eberechi Eze is set to start for England in the clash against Czech Republic tonight. The Arsenal forward is poised to come in for Anthony Gordon, who has started in the three matches during the Nations League international break. Trent Alexander-Arnold is also due to play at right-back, with Jarell Quansah moving to centre-back to cover for Ezri Konsa.

Alex Scott has been ruled out through injury, which has upset Bournemouth after he played in the win over Croatia at the weekend. Myles Lewis-Skelly is expected to get a recall to the team after playing against Czech Republic in Prague last week when England won 2-0. Morgan Rogers, who scored against Croatia, is in line to start in place of Bukayo Saka.

Probable England team: Pickford; Trent, Quansah, Guehi, Hall; Lewis-Skelly, Anderson; Rogers, Bellingham, Eze; Kane

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of England vs Czech Republic from Wembley in the fourth and mercifully final round of fixtures in this sprawling Nations League international break. Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

Shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.

#1249. Man Utd to Make PL Complaint Despite Leny Yoro Red Overturn

Despite having Leny Yoro's red card overturned, following the release of VAR audio which revealed that the defender was wrongly sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity just eight minutes into Manchester United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, the Red Devils are still set to contact the Premier League and ProRef over the controversial decision.

The Red Devils were condemned to their heaviest defeat under a new manager in 100 years on Sunday afternoon, with goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensuring the Reds made full use of their numerical advantage. It also handed Mauricio Pochettino his first real taste of just how difficult his new job is likely to be.

His adopted side now sit 19th in the Premier League table, just one point above bottom-placed Crystal Palace, having managed just one win in their opening 11 league outings.

However, United will feel particularly hard done by after believing their latest fixture was effectively taken out of their hands by referee Sam Barrott and his VAR team, with just eight minutes on the clock.

Despite seeing retrospective action taken to ensure Yoro doesn't serve a suspension, United still think ProRef''s interpretation of the incident is 'totally wrong'.

They view it as both a process error and a failure to interpret the rules correctly. There is disappointment the VAR didn’t challenge the on-field decision, and they don’t see the incident as subjective.

Mauricio Pochettino watched his side go down to ten men after just eight minutes.

Data can be used to show if Isak had maintained his top-recorded speed, he still couldn’t have reached the ball before Senne Lammens. The club plans to raise this with both the Premier League and ProRef directly.

On the VAR audio itself, club insiders - and the top brass - feel there is a quick look and consensus to support the referee with no meaningful challenge or consideration.

Yoro was set to serve a one-match suspension, but it has now been removed after United successfully lodged an appeal for wrongful dismissal. The 21-year-old will now be available to face Brentford on Saturday at Old Trafford.

Debate on whether the foul was a clear denial of a goalscoring opportunity centred on whether Isak would have kept possession of ball as he approached the penalty area. Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations regarding a red card for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO) is the likelihood of the attacking player "keeping or gaining control of the ball" - which is why the FA deemed Sam Barrott's decision to be wrong.

Yet, in the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'D Up, Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb still backed the process of his officials although was non-committal when sharing his own verdict on the incident.

"I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," said Webb. "The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."
