#1196. Sleuth finds ‘impossible proteins’ in hundreds of research papers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured) in cell lines that should not be able to produce them. Credit: Dr Mark J. Winter/SPL

A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines. In these studies, particular proteins show up in imaging experiments, even though the cells do not have the gene necessary to make them.

Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.

“This problem will not go away,” says Thierry Soussi, a cancer geneticist at Uppsala University in Sweden, who notes that there are several other examples of the issue in now-retracted papers that were not included in the sleuth’s analysis. “This is only the tip of a gigantic iceberg.”

Cell lines are groups of cells derived from a single origin cell and cultured for use in experiments. Some cancer cell lines have been genetically modified with mutations and deletions — often to remove genes that usually control cell division. This means that the cultures continually divide and grow, giving researchers the chance to study tumour progression and test potential treatments.

The MCF-7 cell line is one of these. It lacks the gene for caspase-3 protein, which is involved in cell death. In 2009, researchers warned1 that some studies that report working with MCF-7 have mysteriously observed caspase-3 expression in western blots, an imaging technique that identifies proteins on the basis of their molecular weight.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody

In the most recent analysis, published as a preprint on 21 October to the data repository Zenodo2, Sholto David, a sleuth based in Arbroath, UK, finds that this problem persists and extends to other cell lines.

David compiled a list of 20 commonly used cell lines with genetic mutations or deletions that leave cells unable to express specific proteins. He then scoured the literature using Google text and image searches to identify examples of western-blot images that unexpectedly identify these proteins. He also searched a collection of 140,000 articles that he had previously downloaded and screened for image-integrity issues and other problems, most of which were biomedicine papers.

He found 230 reports of phantom proteins across 221 papers published since 2004. The most common errors were observations of caspase-3 expression in the MCF-7 cell line, affecting 49 papers; expression of the cell-death protein BAX in the Jurkat cell line in 47 papers; and expression of the signalling protein STAT3 in the PC-3 cell line in 35 papers.

David suggests several explanations for these impossible protein-expression patterns. They might be the result of honest errors: researchers could have misidentified the cell lines or contaminated them with others. Or the antibodies used to identify proteins in the western-blot experiments could have been non-specific and bound to another protein with the same molecular weight. In fact, David says that he stumbled across the anomalous proteins while working on a project that flagged hundreds of studies that used the wrong antibodies in experiments.

Another possibility is that some of the papers are the product of paper mills, companies that fabricate and sell scientific manuscripts. David says that some papers in the cache contain the hallmarks of being produced by such outfits, including duplicated images or text templates that are similar to other papers. The proportion of the papers that fall into this category is not clear, he says.

Nature has contacted several authors of papers containing anomalies to ask for comment, but none responded.

#1195. Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch

Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

"Heartbroken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real." Those were the words with which Spanish second division football club Tenerife confirmed the death of 30-year-old Jesus de Miguel on Tuesday.

De Miguel was involved in a clash in the middle of the pitch with FC Andorra's Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball with the score 2-2 late in the game. Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.

Spanish media reported that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically" before his death.

After confirming the death on Tuesday morning, the club posted that: "No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news."

Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" as messages of support began to flood in on Tuesday.

"I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media.

Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish FA (RFEF).

"Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today," wrote the federation in a statement.

The RFEF postponed Tuesday's matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina, "as a gesture of respect and solidarity."

De Miguel had been with Tenerife since joining from from Castellon in 2025. He began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023.

#1193. Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he said. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

“It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

All Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. But the hint of self-immolation in Palace’s display should not obscure the swagger of Brighton’s performance. Despite losing Danny Welbeck, last year’s top scorer, Brighton have scored 23 goals already this Premier League campaign, the most in the league. This tally includes one of the most extraordinary goals in Premier League history.

Most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. And so, just as he entered the centre circle in the opposition half, Gómez attempted the absurd.

“I’m not training with Diego Gómez shooting from 50 metres in training,” head coach Fabian Hürzeler said while breaking into a smile. “It’s just about making the players quick in their minds.

“In these moments it’s about being very precise with his long kick. The perception to recognise the keeper and being quick to go to the action was impressive.”

The presence of mind to attempt something outlandish was one thing; the execution was quite another. With Benítez vulnerable, Gómez took just one touch with his right foot before taking his shot, not giving the keeper enough time to scramble back to cover his line. As he looked up to confirm the opportunity, the 23-year-old struck the ball over Benítez with such venom that it did not even bounce until it reached the goal.

All that remained was for the Paraguayan international to hurtle towards the corner flag, engulfed by his ecstatic team-mates. For the Brighton fans, soaked by showers at the Amex, rain can never have felt so sweet.

Gómez’s goal will earn comparisons with David Beckham’s lob from the halfway line at Wimbledon. The advancements in pressing and conditioning in the 30 years since, with space ever more congested, makes such a strike even harder today. Not since Wayne Rooney in 2017 has a player scored a Premier League goal from further out than Gómez’s 56 yards.

Gómez may well attempt an encore. He shot from even further out at the Stadium of Light a week ago. When October ends, three of the last four Premier League goal-of-the-month winners will be Brighton players. Alongside his meticulous emphasis on set-pieces, Hürzeler empowers flair in open play.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

You can also follow the latest updates from Manchester United’s crucial trip to Elland Road in our sister blog here.

#1192. How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community

As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

"Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.

It is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture. The asterisk signals the inclusion of non-Arab ethnic minorities and people with diverse identities and roots in Southwest Asia and North Africa.

Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.

This year's theme, "Who's Your Diva?!," brought together drag performers paying tribute to legendary figures from across the Eastern Mediterranean who have become queer icons — from Egyptian music legend Umm Kulthum to Turkish star Bülent Ersoy and Lebanese pop icon Haifa Wehbe.

Hassandra, co-founder of ADIRA and the ADIRA Drag Festival, was among the performers, taking on the persona of Lebanese pop star Elissa.

"It is very important for me to bring my Lebanese Arab identity and culture into what I do, because I think it's a very beautiful culture. And there's a lot of campy, glamorous, beautiful divas," Hassandra said.

Elissa's "whole discography is very romantic, raw, soft, kind of like very Adele vibes," Hassandra told DW ahead of the October 30 show. "However, her personality is known to be the extreme opposite. She's very feisty. Very blunt, very unfiltered. Not soft at all as a person."

The star is also known for speaking out on political issues in Lebanon. She has publicly voiced support for LGBTQ+ communities in the Middle East, while also frequently sparking controversy across the Arab world with her outspoken positions on other political issues.

Hassandra's ADIRA Drag Festival performance addresses this complexity, ultimately "tapping into her sort of controversial political opinions," the drag artist explained.

This reflects one of the ideas Hassandra hopes to promote with the theme of this year's festival. "As queer people, we tend to idealize a lot of pop divas. But these pop divas are very imperfect in their nature," Hassandra said. The show provides an opportunity to critically revisit these divas' legacy through a more critical lens.

"And this sort of critical lens can be taken into the outside world, as in: never follow anyone in life blindly. No one should follow any politician, any political party, any pop diva, any activist blindly."

Born in Beirut in 1994, Hassandra studied theater and stage acting at the Lebanese University before moving to Berlin in 2017. "I would say it was it was just a very sort of impulsive decision at the age of 22. I mean, there's no doubt that the economic situation was really bad in Lebanon and continued to become even worse," the artist said.

In Berlin, Hassandra became increasingly involved in the city's independent art scene and queer nightlife. Drag emerged as another form of self-expression for the actor.

Through performances that combine theatrical intensity, political humor, grotesque aesthetics and moments of tenderness, Hassandra challenges conventional understandings of gender and identity.

Their work explores themes of home, nostalgia, displacement and queer Arab culture. These ideas are also central to ADIRA, which Hassandra founded in 2023 with Syrian-German DJ and cultural producer Zuher Jazmati, also known as xanax_attax.

Through panel discussions, performances and music events, ADIRA fosters collective participation and community-building.

As Islamophobia and homophobia rise alongside the far right, spaces like ADIRA offer a sense of belonging and support for Arab queer communities.

That sense of community has become even more important following the deadly Islamist terrorist attack during Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride parade in July.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In the aftermath, Hassandra felt caught between their different identities. As an Arab queer person, "you fall in this position where then you start receiving a lot of racism," they said.

"And I think this is why it's important, for us queer Arabs, to say we are sad over what happened, but that we also reject any of the racism that comes from that," Hassandra said. "I think we [the Arab community] are being used in a lot of ways as a punching bag for a lot of things that are happening."

Rather than allowing the attack to fuel hatred and racism, Hassandra said, "we should make Germany a safer place for everyone to live in."  "There's place for everyone. It's a huge country," they added.

The interview with Hassandra was conducted by Gönna Ketels.

#1191. UCL | Como 1-0 AEK Athens: Milla magic cancels out Da Cunha miss

The Luis Milla curler into the far top corner proved enough for Como to see off AEK Athens and surge towards the Champions League Round of 16, despite Lucas Da Cunha’s missed penalty.

The Lariani had won three of their first four Champions League games, despite missing Moise Kean and Assane Diao, with Maxence Caqueret not at 100 per cent either, but Trevoh Chalobah returned five weeks after his muscular injury.

AEK Athens lost their last three in Europe, but were leading Real Madrid twice until capitulating 3-2 in stoppages. Aboubakary Koita was sent off for dissent and therefore suspended, with midfielder Kervin Arriaga injured, but ex-Lazio goalkeeper Thomas Strakosha made his Champions League debut for this season after a wrist sprain.

Lazaros Rota made a decisive defensive block to stop Tasos Douvikas meeting the Nico Paz through ball at full stretch, then Stavros Pilios got back to block Nico Paz on the counter, but the Argentine was booked for flailing an elbow into the defender’s face.

There were a few technical problems with the referee’s communication system, both before kick-off and during the first half, but he didn’t need help from VAR when Lovro Majer was very late to trip Alex Valle in the box.

However, Lucas Da Cunha slipped a little in the run-up and fired the penalty off target for Como. It was the first time in his career that the France international had failed to convert from the spot.

Jacobo Ramon couldn’t keep his header down from eight yards, and Alex Valle wasted a promising move with his scuffed finish past the near post.

Robert Sanchez needed a huge double save on the stroke of half-time, first on the Mijat Gacinovic deflected effort, then the Rota rebound too.

AEK had a huge chance after the restart, but Milan Vitalis couldn’t keep the finish down under pressure from a promising position after doing such good work to get into that situation.

Luis Milla with an unbelievable strike to give Como the lead 🥵

Como survived the scares and took the lead when Luis Milla bent a right-foot curler into the far top corner from outside the area, on the Martin Baturina lay-off.

Nico Paz so nearly made it 2-0 when AEK gave it away playing out from the back, so Valle sent the Argentine through to clip the base of the near post.

Jacobo Ramon’s header was just wide on a free kick, with the same for the Moukoudi attempt on a free kick from ex-Cagliari midfielder Razvan Marin.

Maxi Perrone had a great chance to add another in the final minute, but was denied by a desperate one-handed Strakosha save.

#1190. Man United Confidential: Carrington crash adds to Mauricio Pochettino's woes, as new boss set to cut players' days off... and why the wait goes on for coach Silvia Tuya

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 12:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:16 EST, 24 November 2026

As if having his first training session as Manchester United head coach sabotaged by a drone wasn’t dramatic enough, Mauricio Pochettino’s second day at work saw access to the club’s training base blocked by a serious road accident.

The collision between a vehicle and a cyclist on one of the two approaches to Carrington, where United’s players and staff are regularly seen driving through a security checkpoint, meant it was closed off for several hours on Friday while an ambulance and police cars attended the scene.

Greater Manchester Police say the cyclist was taken to hospital to receive treatment for injuries that were not life-threatening and no arrests were made.

However, anyone leaving Carrington had to take an alternative route in the opposite direction. That included the players after training and Pochettino and his staff following his first pre-match press conference.

The accident on Friday completed an eventful 48 hours at Carrington after a rogue drone operator filmed 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first training session and posted it on YouTube. He later took the video down and apologised for the intrusion, which United sources said was the right thing to do – even though they had not contacted the uploader directly and do not intend to take legal action against him.

They insisted there was not a breach of security at Carrington, but claimed a number of laws had been broken. Insiders promised a robust response to any further incidents to protect the rights of the club and its staff, and warned that those responsible would be ‘exposing themselves to significant legal and financial risk’.

It's been a testing first few days for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United boss

One of the unexpected issues to hamper the Argentine was a drone filming his first training session

Meanwhile, players leaving Carrington last Friday had to take an alternative route after a serious road accident near United's training ground

Confidential understands Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems as soon as possible.

The squad were pictured arriving around 8.30am as they looked to regroup after the 4-0 hammering at Anfield and begin their preparations for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal on Wednesday night.

The Argentine is eager to spend as much time as possible with the players on the training ground, having only taken over as United boss last Wednesday – four days before the Liverpool clash.

United now face 11 games in 43 days and sources believe there may not be too many days off as Pochettino tries to haul his team out of the relegation zone and ensure qualification for the knockout stage of the Champions League.

At least the indications are that he will allow the players to stay at home the night before games at Old Trafford, rather than having them cooped up in a hotel like some previous United managers.

Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems

Matheus Cunha won’t play any part against Sporting following his red card in United's last Champions League tie against Roma three weeks ago.

Confidential has learned the Brazilian was set to claim the player of the match award after scoring two late goals in the 3-2 win over Roma, only for UEFA to step in.

UEFA rules prevent a player who has been sent off from receiving the award and so the selector – in this case Steve Cooper, the former Leicester, Nottingham Forest and Swansea boss who is now one of the governing body's technical observers – was forced into a late switch, picking Bruno Fernandes instead.

Cunha’s absence will be keenly felt in Portugal. He played no part in Tuesday’s training session at Carrington, instead working on his own in the gym.

At a time when United have the most porous defence in Europe’s top five leagues and Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven are all struggling for form, Pochettino is going to need Harry Maguire.

Pochettino overlooked the experienced Englishman from the start for the trip to Anfield but ended the match with Maguire on the pitch and he was United’s best defender on another desperate afternoon.

Maguire is walking the tightrope of a ban as he remains on four yellow cards after 11 league games. Players are hit with a one-match ban once they receive five or more yellows prior to the conclusion of the 19th league game of the season – eight matches from now.

Even after Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned on appeal, Pochettino can ill-afford to be without Maguire going forward.

Pochettino is going to need the experience of Harry Maguire to hold his defence together but he faces a ban if he is booked again

United are still waiting to see if Pochettino’s strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya can join his staff at Carrington despite hiring new fitness coach Sam Wilson.

Wilson has joined United following his departure from Parma in October, having only moved to the Italian club as head of performance in the summer after 12 years at Arsenal.

It is understood Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team because she is waiting to see if a work permit will be approved.

She joined the US national team staff in October 2024 shortly after Pochettino, and travelled with him, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and analyst Alec Scott when they flew from Cincinnati to Manchester by private jet last week.

Strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team

Some of the early changes under Pochettino have been more subtle than others. Observant fans may have noticed that when the club announced the team to face Liverpool at 3.15pm on Sunday, it was in positional order.

Previously, United’s line-up has been listed numerically, leaving fans to deliberate over the formation. But Pochettino liked to name his team positionally at Tottenham and Chelsea, and admitted in a Q&A on MUTV last week that he wants to do the same at United.

It was clear from the club’s social media post on Sunday that Pochettino would be sticking to the 4-3-2-1 formation favoured by Michael Carrick, with Patrick Dorgu returning on the left wing and Cunha leading the attack.

Not that it lasted very long, as Pochettino admitted he was forced to put his game plan ‘in the bin’ inside eight minutes when Yoro was sent off.

This weekend’s match-up between United and Brentford brings together the most ill-disciplined English team in all competitions and the dirtiest team in the Premier League.

No English team has had more players sent off this season than United’s four – Yoro twice, Cunha against Roma and Martinez against Chelsea.

Meanwhile, Brentford are bottom of the Premier League’s disciplinary 'points table' thanks to their three red cards and 22 yellow cards. So expect referee Rob Jones to be a busy man on Pochettino’s home debut.

Leny Yoro brings down Alexander Isak at Anfield and is sent off - his second red card of the season

Richard Arnold, who preceded Omar Berrada as United's chief executive, pocketed a £5.53m pay-off to stand down after Ineos moved into the club

While Omar Berrada found himself back in the firing line last weekend, the man he succeeded as United’s chief executive was cutting a much more relaxed figure.

Richard Arnold, who led United between February 2022 and December 2023, was spotted enjoying himself on Chester’s popular Eastgate Street on Saturday night – 24 hours before a beleaguered Berrada watched United’s 4-0 thrashing 30 miles down the road at Anfield.

After stepping up to replace Ed Woodward, Arnold was in charge of United for the period spanning United’s strategic review which led to Sir Jim Ratcliffe acquiring 29 per cent of the club. Once it became clear that Ineos would take over the day-to-day running of United, he accepted a £5.53million pay-off to stand down, with the club’s general counsel Patrick Stewart stepping in on an interim basis.

Arnold is now enjoying a quieter life as an executive director at Norton Motorcycles and, it would appear, nights out close to his home near Chester.

It was there that he met a group of United protesters outside his local pub in June 2022 and admitted that the last 12 months had been ‘a f****** nightmare’ and United had ‘f****** burned through cash’. Nothing much seems to have changed since then.

#1189. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area showed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”

It’s all over at Elland Road, with Leeds and Man Utd playing out a competitive draw. Mbeumo’s opener was cancelled out by Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser in a game that was low on attacking quality and chances. Ultimately, a draw was a very fair reflection of the match. Man Utd are 14th and winless in six games across all competitions, while Leeds move into the top seven.

Unconvincing goalkeeping from Lammens as he only punches Ampadu’s cross as far as Stach, whose tame shot squeezes through the Belgian’s legs. However, it’s blocked by the Man Utd defence and Lammens eventually gathers the ball.

There will be four minutes of added time. Can either side snatch a late victory?

Three times now United have looked like they’re about to get away down the flanks in the last few minutes and each time they’ve been flagged offside (Amad twice, Mbeumo once) and each occasion the player was able to look across the line. Carrick looked to the heavens. And he’s right to be frustrated. So avoidable.

Nmecha and Maguire challenge for the ball in the air, with the Man Utd defender bumping into the back of the Leeds substitute’s head. The crowd half-heartedly appeal for a penalty, but it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR.

Carrick responds with a positive, attacking switch as Tielemans departs for Cunha.

Farke makes another change for Leeds as Longstaff replaces Tanaka in midfield.

Excellently goalkeeping from Trafford, who dashes out of his six-yard box to collect Andrey Santos’ pass and keep the ball in his grasp while staying in his box under the watchful eye of Mbeumo.

Dalot drives forward and leads a counter-attack. He passes to Amad, who forces a corner as Leeds get back well and recover. Man Utd take a clever short corner routine, but it ends with Mount scuffing an effort wide.

From presentable range, Fernandes curls an effort straight into Trafford’s arms. Dalot then fails to adequately deal with a cross, heading the ball only as far as Stach. However, the Leeds midfielder wildly lashes his strike over the bar.

United were under that cosh in that period after Leeds equalised but they’ve gained a foothold back in the game now and a bit of frustration has crept in among the home fans. Stach the third player to fire high over the bar. Could go either way this.

How much longer will Carrick wait before making some changes in forward areas? His side need some renewed attacking impetus. The Man Utd head coach has Rashford, Cunha, Mount and Zirkzee all on the bench to choose from.

Okafor attempts to spearhead a Leeds break by playing in Calvert-Lewin. However, his pass is poor and it’s intercepted by Maguire. Amad is down after being caught by Tanaka earlier in that phase of play.

On the turn, Fernandes drags a low effort wide of the far post in a rare attacking flurry for Man Utd in this second half.

Ampadu feels Leeds should have a penalty as he collides with Maguire at a corner. The Man Utd defender hauls the Leeds captain to the floor. It’s been checked and cleared by VAR, but Maguire was taking a huge risk there.

Michael Carrick will surely be angry at the way Manchester United have started the second-half. Leeds now on top and a huge few minutes ahead for Carrick.

Gudmundsson’s searching cross can’t quite find Calvert-Lewin as Man Utd scramble it clear. The away side’s backline has three defenders playing out of position, and they’ve been made to pay by Leeds’ leveller.

Calvert-Lewin attempts to latch onto Bogle’s clipped cross, but he directs it harmlessly wide.

Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and said he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

With all eyes on the visitors, Leeds will be licking their lips at the prospect of piling further misery on their beleaguered opponents. Daniel Farke’s side suffered their first Premier League loss last weekend, falling 2-1 to Arsenal at the Emirates after going a goal up, but the mood remains positive after a solid start to the campaign.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

This has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1188. Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

In this plot of the Riemann ζ function on the complex plane, every point represents a complex number, with the real part plotted on the horizontal axis (from −10 to 10) and the imaginary part on the vertical axis (also from −10 to 10). The colours represent the output of the function, with the junctions where the hues converge around a point showing some of the all-important zeroes.Credit: Empetrisor via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

In a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field. But on the same day as the Anthropic claim, a separate study claiming to have proven the Riemann also emerged — and this one is entirely human written.

The Anthropic announcement came on 20 November from Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the San Francisco, California, company. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote, referring to Anthropic’s large language model (LLM).

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

“If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a winner of the Fields Medal — mathematics’ most prestigious prize — at the University of Oxford, UK.

Hours later, Ravi Vakil, a mathematician at Stanford University in California, posted a rival preprint to Alpöge’s online, in what Vakil called a “hurried announcement” of a proof that “is all human, with no AI”. The preprint was written by Alessandro Maria Masullo, a mathematician who received his PhD at Stanford in 2020 under the supervision of number theorist Brian Conrad. “The hope was to have Brian work with Alessandro for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people,” Vakil wrote. “Now it seems best to put out the current draft.”

The confirmation of either or both solutions would be a spectacular bicentenary present for Bernhard Riemann, the German mathematician who was born 200 years ago this September and who formulated the problem, which addresses the distribution of prime numbers, in the mid-1800s.

The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which has its scientific headquarters in Oxford, UK, at the turn of the twenty-first century. The institute offers a US$1 million prize to anyone who devises a solution to one of the problems, which are considered some of the most challenging in the field. Mathematicians using AI tools announced earlier this year that they had solved another Millennium problem, related to the Navier-Stokes equation.

The problem has to do with the ‘Riemann ζ function’ (ζ is the Greek letter zeta), which encodes the randomness properties of the prime numbers. Riemann discovered that the distribution of primes is encoded in the ζ function’s ‘zeroes’. These are points, denoted by z, on a plane satisfying the equation ζ(z) = 0.

Riemann conjectured that apart from some obvious but uninteresting cases, all such solutions had to lie on a certain vertical line in the plane. If this were true, he showed, it would imply that prime numbers are scattered among all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as random as it could be.

The Riemann hypothesis has been a lodestar for generations of mathematicians. Credit: James Brittain/Getty

Alpöge’s four-page document includes a sketch of the proof. But Andrew Granville, a number theorist at the University of Montreal in Canada, says that Alpöge should have taken the time to prepare a clearer write-up before making the announcement, which came just days after Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO). The IPO initially valued the company at US$1.5 trillion, but the company’s valuation dropped on 19 November.

“What he released is garbled,” Granville says of Alpöge’s document. Granville cites the downturn in the company’s stock value as the reason for the timing of the proof’s release.

“There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false,” Alpöge wrote in the document.

Anthropic did not respond immediately to Nature’s request for comment.

Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University who collaborated with Alpöge on a separate project regarding the Navier-Stokes equation, says that Alpöge deserves a lot of credit for developing techniques to produce mathematical results using LLMs. “Levent himself built this amazing set-up to do math.” He adds that Alpöge, who is himself a number theorist on leave from Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been working relentlessly for months on this and other problems, hardly ever getting any sleep.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

“I suspect that the proof will turn out to be correct,” Maynard says of the Alpöge announcement, even though it is now in the form of incomprehensible code in the Lean programming language.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03812-7

#1187. 'Moments aren't enough': Inside Ethan Nwaneri's struggles on loan at Borussia Dortmund ahead of his return to the Emirates tonight - as Arsenal face dilemma over talented youngster suffering crisis of confidence

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he said.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’

There's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ says Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’

'He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play,' says Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against New Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

#1186. Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a big moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke said. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”

Forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Murillo had Forest’s best opportunity two minutes into injury time after cutting inside the penalty area but could not find the top corner.

"That was magic!" What a goal this would have been from Murillo?! 😩 https://t.co/D07lB7hN47

Another defeat will only add to their concerns and Glasner needs to quickly find a solution or face another relegation battle.

It does not promise to get easier immediately, either, with Manchester City, Chelsea and Brighton up next in the league at home, but there were encouraging signs here, despite the club sitting in the bottom three.

Glasner said: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

“It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”

We knew the margins would be really small. They are extremely well coached and organised. The longer the game goes on they gain more belief. We had to be so patient - and clinical when we got the chance. The way they were defending, they were more comfortable. But we have players with different qualities and can adapt to what the game is delivering.

We have another three big chances that should be goals. That is the difference, you have to be clinical. If we keep generating them, they will come.

Let’s enjoy the win, because it was a very tough one. And then, on Wednesday, we have an incredible game against Bayern Munich away [in the Champions League].

When you see their goal it’s deflected otherwise, it’s straight to the gloves of Matz Sels. You have periods in football where you feel everything going against you and then there are periods when things are on your side.

Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.

And having this coolness, not to worry too much because I can see good performances and not good results. The results will come if the performances stay good.

Arsenal building some pressure, and they have another corner. Arteta signalling that he wants to make the change before the corner is taken and here come the changes: White for Timber, Havertz for Gyokeres and Merino on for Bruno Guimaraes.

Gabriel meets Rice’s delivery, but he fails to direct his header on target.

Excellent defending from Gabriel up against Ndoye in the right channel, but it was another promising moment for Forest in this second half. Madueke then isolates his man one-on-one, and wins another corner.

Timber, Merino and Gyokeres are all ready to come on for Arsenal.

The game is see-sawing, Arsenal have a corner after Calafiori fed Madueke down the left and his cross was blocked. Sels punches away, and then Odegaard loses some patience and tries to find Calafiori with a pass that is not on.

Saka and Rice lose duels when fishing for fouls and Forest have another corner. Arsenal’s performance level has certainly not improved since half-time.

Arsenal clear, but Odegaard blocks a cross and Forest win a second corner in quick succession. Excellent goalkeeping from Raya to claim, and he bowls the ball forward quickly, but Forest snuff out the danger against Madueke.

The first half was an attack against defence session for long periods but Arsenal know they are in an arm wrestle now. Forest far more aggressive, and the crowd are more involved. But that could open up avenues of space. White with a really poor pass towards Saka which is astray.

Arsenal have a corner of their own after breaking from Raya’s gloves. Much more open game so far.

Forest deal with Saka’s delivery, and there was a very brief VAR check for a handball penalty. Nothing doing.

Madueke looking dangerous, receiving a Gabriel ball over the top and dashing inside but his shot was blocked.

The winger then tried to make amends, but he gave away a free-kick at the expense of a booking.

Delap’s shot from a tight angle is then deflected wide. Forest corner, from which Murillo’s header loops into Raya’s gloves. Forest showing more attacking ambition.

Liam Delap is producing a very decent centre-forward performance.

The £50m record signing is proving a real threat with his power and running.

Madueke and Rice not one the same wavelength, before Delap does well to win a shoulder to shoulder with Gabriel only to slice his cross behind for an Arsenal goal kick. Sums up the lack of attacking quality in the game.

Forest have another free-kick in a shooting position after Havertz is penalised for blocking a long shot with his hand. McAtee’s effort from the free-kick is scooped miles over the bar.

Both teams looking livelier in the early exchanges of the half, but Forest’s counter-attack was the more dangerous, with Liam Delap doing well to hold on to the ball and whipping a cross into the box that was just ahead of Williams.

Noni Madueke replaces Eberechi Eze, so a more natural wide player on his stronger foot on Arsenal’s left flank.

Frustrating first half for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta will be demanding more from his attacking players.

Arsenal have not registered a shot on target so far and their delivery from set-pieces has been poor.

Forest look relatively comfortable and had the best chance of the half with a shot from Dan Ndoye which was saved by David Raya.

Are we heading for a hat-trick of 0-0 draws at the City Ground between these two teams?

A very uneventful 45 minutes which has been played at the pace of a pre-season game at times. Similarities with the last two fixtures between these teams at the City Ground, and Arsenal’s games against Leeds and Lille this week. They put their foot on the pedal after half-time in both games, and they need to do the same here.

Guimaraes is off the pitch, and there will be more than two minutes added now as a result of his treatment. Forest win a corner, but Havertz heads away at the near post.

Just the two minutes of added time to play.

Liam Delap wins a free-kick in a shooting position for Forest after Arsenal were caught with numbers forward. Big moment for the home team, this. Calafiori was caught on the ball again, he has not had the best of games.

Williams and McAtee are over the free keek, which is around 25 yards out, left of centre.

Williams blasts the ball into Bruno Guimaraes, who goes down and stays down after taking the shot flush in the face.

More incisive from Arsenal, with Rice punching the ball into Odegaard and then on to Havertz but the angle was always against him and the German could only shoot into the side-netting. Forest have defended very well, overall. Although they have been deep for the most part, they have jumped and pushed out at the right times to stop Arsenal accessing the box.

Glasner and Arteta dish out some instruction while there is a stoppage in play to deal with a hand in the face that troubled Schlager. Can either side find a breakthrough before the break?

David Raya claimed that Forest corner with ease and the game has now resumed its pattern. Forest retreating into their shape, and Arsenal passing in front of them. Schlager penalised for a foul on Saka, the home fans not happy with the decision, I think because Saka was going away from goal.

Rice clips in a menacing delivery, but Havertz skewed his header wide from seven or eight yards. Good chance, Arsenal’s best so far.

More Arsenal probing but the small details are letting them down: Eze’s return to Odegaard forced his team-mate to check, and then Odegaard’s touch was heavy after a wall pass from Guimaraes.

Delap does well to make a nuisance of himself at the other end, and his long-range shot deflects behind for a corner.

Strong from Konsa to win the ball, drive out of defence and win a foul. Rice with a well-weighted scoop over the Forest defence for the run of Ben White, but he skewed his cross behind for a goal kick.

Arsenal with another corner. No doubt they have been the game’s dominant force when it comes to possession and territory, but there has been a lack of cutting edge so far. Saka goes for the near post again but Forest deal with it. The home crowd groan at Sels for not releasing the ball quickly in search of a break.

Arsenal work the ball across their midfield with Guimaraes, Rice and Odegaard all involved, and a dangerous Saka cross is headed behind for a corner.

Scramble! The near-post flick on caused chaos and Konsa’s goal-bound backheel was blocked, but the ball would not quite drop for Ben White to score a tap-in.

After two successive goalless draws here between the two clubs, this is following a similar script so far.

It’s a very tight affair with Arsenal enjoying more of the possession but Forest seemingly happy with that and content to them on the break.

Bruno Guimaraes has made a bright start for the visitors.

Forest’s best attacking moment of the game and it comes from an Arsenal mistake.

Calafiori just had to play a five-yard pass back to Gabriel but scuffed it, and Munoz pounced. Running at the Arsenal penalty area, Munoz’s cross was deflected to the back post and the ball found it’s way to Ndoye. Decent reverse shot through legs, but Raya had it covered and tipped around the post.

From the corner, Forest are penalised for a foul.

Arsenal continue to have Forest penned in their own half, very difficult for the home team to play through the midfield or over Konsa and Gabriel so far.

Saka produces his first successful dribble to beat Williams, and the left wing-back trips him at the expense of a free-kick and a booking. Rice’s delivery from the right was uncharacteristically poor.

Munoz tries to drag Forest up the pitch to apply some pressure on Arsenal but he is penalised for a shirt pull on Gabriel. The atmosphere sounds pretty sleepy, a result of some tepid Arsenal possession and Forest’s bad home record.

Forest making sure they have numbers around Saka whenever Arsenal funnel attacks down their right, which is almost always their preferred side.

Neat from Guimaraes in midfield to turn and find Saka with some earlier service, and Sels tips his cross away from danger.

Delap and Ndoye waiting for a slip-up or counter-attack but they are feeding on scraps at the moment. Arsenal yet to carve out a proper chance, though.

It’s already pretty clear that one of the key duels today will be between Gabriel and Liam Delap.

Forest’s record signing Delap has already let Gabriel know he’s in the game with his physicality.

Cute pass from Bruno Guimaraes to break the Forest midfield line and find Odegaard, but strangely the Arsenal captain could not sort his feet out to control the ball and back a clean pass. Then Williams defends well against Saka from an Arsenal attacking transition.

Pretty subdued start from Forest. The crowd’s spirits were raised there by Delap chasing down Konsa who had the deal with the sun his eyes, but the Forest striker pushed him in the back.

Arsenal enjoying all of the possession so far, and most of it has come in Forest’s half. One or two players on Arsenal’s right/Forest’s left struggling with the low evening sun. Havertz did get in behind but his cross into the middle was too strong.

Arsenal get the game under way, and play short from kick-off.

There will be a degree of pressure on birthday boy James McAtee today to make an impression.

With Morgan Gibbs-White injured, McAtee is likely to take the No 10 position and continue his redemption arc.

McAtee has been revitalised since the arrival of Oliver Glasner and this is a big afternoon for the former England under 21 international.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

An FA Cup defeat in Jan 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparked a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

Yet Arsenal have secured two wins in a row since that defeat at Brighton, without being truly at their fluent best, and will be confident against a Forest team without injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White.
